i0: ***Have got*** means the same as ***have*** for **possession**, **family**, **appearance** and **illness**: *I**'ve got** two sisters. She**'s got** blue eyes. I**'ve got** a cold.* It's very common in **British** English, especially in speech.
i1: In American English, people usually say *I have* and *Do you have…?* Both are correct. For *have to* (obligation), see [Must and Have To](/blog/grammar/must-have-to/).
hg-forms.s: ***I / you / we / they have got*** ('ve got). ***He / she / it has got*** ('s got). Use it for things you **own**, **family**, **appearance** and **illness**.
hg-forms.b1: ***He's got*** = *he has got* (not *he is got*). The context tells you: *He's got a dog* (has) / *He's tired* (is).
hg-neg-q.t: I haven't got, have you got…?
hg-neg-q.s: **Negative**: ***haven't got / hasn't got***. **Questions**: ***Have you got…? Has she got…?*** Short answers: *Yes, I have. No, she hasn't.* (not *Yes, I've got*)
hg-neg-q.b1: Don't use *do* with *have got*: ***Have** you got…?* (not *Do you have got…?*)
hg-or-have.t: Have got or have? Have breakfast, had a car
hg-or-have.s: ***Have got*** and ***have*** mean the same for **possession**. But use only ***have*** for **actions** (*have breakfast, have a shower, have a party*) and in the **past** (*I had a bike*, not *I had got a bike*).
hg-or-have.b0.0.0: *I've got a car. / I have a car.*
hg-or-have.b0.1.0: *Have you got a pen? / Do you have a pen?*
hg-or-have.b0.2.0: *She's got a cold. / She has a cold.*
hg-or-have.b0.2.1: *I **had** a bike when I was a child.* (past)
hg-or-have.b0.3.1: *I usually **have** a shower in the morning.* (habit)
hg-or-have.b1: With ***have*** (not *have got*), questions and negatives use ***do***: ***Do** you **have** a car? I **don't have** time.*
hg-got-to.t: Have got to, got and gotten
hg-got-to.s: ***Have got to*** + verb = ***have to*** (obligation, informal): *I**'ve got to** go.* In American English, the past participle of *get* is often ***gotten*** (*It's gotten cold*), but ***have got*** (possession) is the same in both.
hg-got-to.b1: ***Have got to*** is for the **present** and **future**. For the past, use ***had to***: *I **had to** work late yesterday.* (not *I had got to*)
hg-got-to.b2: ***Gotta*** = *(have) got to* in very informal speech and songs. Don't use it in writing.
